findings.text: WindowNavigator restores or assigns navigation focus before the required lifecycle boundary. _resume calls _SetNavigationActive(true) before the synchronous Resume hook, so a window without BlockObjectRef selects its default before Resume completes. _commit likewise activates navigation before _transition acquires the Open token, causing an observable premature selection even with a valid blocker and leaving focus active throughout Open when the reference is absent. PRD-REQ-183/187 and PRD-AC-080/081/083/084 require Resume/Open completion before eligibility/focus restoration.

Open-failure cleanup results are still discarded. Both _add and the replacement Open-failure branch call _dispose(...) without using its boolean result, so an ordinary Open failure whose Clear/destroy/pool release also fails returns OpenFailed instead of CleanupFailed. The approved cleanup contract requires CleanupFailed whenever any cleanup/destroy/release step fails; the new replacement test covers only cleanup failure of the removed old window, not cleanup failure of the failed new candidate.

The function registered as TS-TEST-004/005/008 multi-window lifecycle does not implement the mandatory TS-TEST-008 Pause/Resume partitions. It has no custom Pause or Resume override, no isolated hook-error case, no yielding-hook closed-thread fixture, and no paused-view custom-method proof, despite technical-specification TS-TEST-008 and SLICE-003's mandatory automated identity requiring those deterministic checks. The current happy-path and Open/Close recovery assertions therefore cannot honestly establish the claimed TS-TEST-008 lifecycle coverage.
